records.stem: ww Which of the following clinical features would you least expect to see in a lesion of the frontal lobe:
options: Conjugate eye deviation towards side of lesion (x) Contralateral weakness of the face and arm 5%
records.explanation: Loss of two-point discrimination is most likely to occur in a lesion of the parietal lobe. Expressive dysphasia results from damage to Broca's area. Contralateral weakness of the face and arm results from damage to the primary motor cortex. Personality change results from damage to the prefrontal cortex. Conjugate eye deviation towards side of lesion results from damage to the frontal eye field. : v Frontal Lobe

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: ww Damage to Broca's area will most likely result in which of the following clinical features:
records.explanation: The Broca's speech area, in the frontal lobe of the dominant hemisphere, is the ‘expressive’ centre for the production of speech. It is connected to the Wernicke's speech area by the arcuate fasciculus. Damage to this area will result in an expressive dysphasia. Vv Frontal Lobe ANATOMY / CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: ww A 40 year old female presents to ED complaining of complete visual loss in her right eye. On fundoscopy you note a pale retina and a cherry red spot. You suspect an emboli. Which of the following blood vessels is most likely the source of the emboli:
options: Anterior cerebral artery (x) Middl cerebral artery 8%
Posterior cerebral artery (Vv) Internal carotid artery 56%
records.explanation: The internal carotid artery is the most likely source of the emboli. The ophthalmic artery arises from the internal carotid artery and supplies structures in the orbit and eyeball. The central retinal artery is the most important branch of the ophthalmic artery, supplying the retina and the optic disc. The central retinal artery is an end artery that does not anastomose with other arteries, and thus its occlusion results in monocular blindness. : Vv
